solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Diver maybe raised rocks protecting bar mouth

indicators.note: the jumbled letters surround and shield the next piece
to rock is to shake or disturb, so the letters of raised are jumbled
the mouth of something is its opening, so only the opening letter of bar is used

explanation.surface: A description of raised rocks guarding the entrance to a sandbar at a river mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' scrambles RAISED, and 'protecting' wraps that round B, the 'mouth' of bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A diver is a type of bird that feeds at sea, so it is one example of the wider class.

clue.text: Small Russian leader's pointless climbing exercises

indicators.note: climbing in a down entry means the letters read upwards
pointless means without a compass point, so the letter for north drops out

parts.note: Putin is the Russian leader, with the possessive giving a final S

explanation.surface: A minor Russian leader's exercise routine goes nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointless' removes N (north) from S PUTINS; 'climbing' turns SPUTIS upwards to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: These are floor exercises in which one raises the trunk from lying to sitting.

clue.text: Big merchant, Scottish chap, forest dweller

parts.note: Amazon is a huge online retailer
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A list of three people: a big trader, a Scotsman, a woodland resident.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living in the Amazon rainforest is an inhabitant of that jungle region.

clue.text: Bunch of schoolgirls erect house up north

indicators.note: erect means standing upright, so in a down answer the letters read upwards
a bunch of the word means some of its letters taken together

explanation.surface: Some schoolgirls put up a house in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunch of' takes OOLGI from 'schoolgirls'; 'erect' turns it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An Inuit snow dome is a dwelling built in the Arctic, far to the north.

clue.text: It could be worth chopping the same business TV series

indicators.note: chopping means cutting into, so the rearranged letters split the other pieces

parts.note: DO is short for ditto, meaning the same
CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: could be means the letters of worth may take another form

explanation.surface: A thought that cutting the same firm might be worthwhile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' reads as part of the surface but is only a link; 'could be' signals the anagram, and 'chopping' says those mixed letters split the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the long-running BBC science-fiction programme about a time-travelling alien.

clue.text: Butterfly gives a firm nip on the outside

indicators.note: says the bite word sits round the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a nip is a small bite, as is a peck
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A butterfly seems to give a business a quick bite from outside.
explanation.definitionFit: The peacock is a well-known European butterfly species with eyespots on its wings.

clue.text: Latin-American suppresses his terror

indicators.note: suppresses means holds back or removes, so these letters go

parts.note: Hispanic describes someone of Latin-American origin

explanation.surface: A man from Latin America hides his fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is sudden overwhelming fear, close in meaning to terror.

clue.text: A lot of chianti, pastis, olives and tapas perhaps

indicators.note: a lot of means a large part, but not all, of these words' letters

explanation.surface: A boozy Mediterranean spread of wine, aniseed spirit, olives and small plates.
explanation.walkthrough: Pastis is a French aniseed-flavoured spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Olives and tapas are examples of the small starters served before an Italian main meal.

clue.text: Circle late notice Republican sent in

indicators.note: sent in means placed inside the death notice

parts.note: an obit is a notice of a death, about the late person

explanation.surface: Someone circles a late notice that a Republican has submitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' here means dead, not overdue.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbit is a curved path round a planet, close to a circle.

clue.text: Stoned after joint not far from the ground

indicators.note: after means the drug word comes later than the joint

parts.note: the knee is a joint of the leg
stoned means intoxicated by drugs, high

explanation.surface: Someone stoned after smoking a joint, lying near the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests cannabis but is the body's joint.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaching only to the knee, so very low and close to floor level.

clue.text: Labour needs a victor to follow

indicators.note: needs in the sense of lacks or goes without, so these letters are removed

parts.note: travail is hard labour or toil
Victor is V in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A political line: the Labour party needs a winner to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' means 'is without': TRAVAIL loses A and V.
explanation.definitionFit: To trail someone is to shadow or track them, keeping behind.

clue.text: Beat copper wire frames on street

indicators.note: to frame something is to surround it, so the wire word goes round the rest

parts.note: a cable is a heavy wire

explanation.surface: Someone beats copper wire into frames along a street, metalworking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat copper' is a police officer on the beat, not hammered metal; 'copper' is British slang for a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A police officer patrolling a beat holds the rank of police constable in Britain.

clue.text: New zoo to cut reduced cost of tiny animals

indicators.note: cut means the shortened cost word is split open by the other letters
reduced means shortened, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: price means cost

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters of zoo to

explanation.surface: A new zoo slashes its admission price for viewing tiny animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' clips the last letter off the cost word, 'New' is the anagram signal, and 'cut' places those mixed letters inside the shortened word.
explanation.definitionFit: Protozoic relates to protozoa, single-celled microscopic organisms once classed as minute animals.

clue.text: Sort of pine, soft pine

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for soft
to pine for something is to long or itch for it

explanation.surface: A list entry: a kind of pine tree, then a soft pine.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'pine' is the verb meaning long for, not the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitch pine is a resinous American conifer, so the word names one variety of the tree.

clue.text: Means to view plaster facade

parts.note: a window is a way to look out or in
a plaster is a dressing for a wound

explanation.surface: A builder discussing how to see a plastered front wall of a house.
explanation.definitionFit: Both terms describe a misleading show put on to impress, a pretence covering what lies beneath.

clue.text: Discourage writer's resolve

parts.note: to discourage is to deter
the setter's own, so the writer's means mine

explanation.surface: Putting off an author's determination.
explanation.definitionFit: To resolve on something is to decide it firmly, as when you settle a question.

clue.text: Batsman whips Swedes, say

parts.note: Joe Root is an England cricket batsman
crops are short riding whips

explanation.surface: An England batsman thrashes Swedish cricketers.
explanation.walkthrough: A swede is a root vegetable (rutabaga), not a Scandinavian.
explanation.definitionFit: Swedes are one example of vegetables grown for their swollen edible underground parts.

clue.text: Work at airline, among other things

indicators.note: to work something is to shape or process it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An employee lists their duties at an airline, among other things.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase is used in English to mean amongst various others.

clue.text: Like approach taken by hospital with treatment of colitis?

definitions.text: Like approach taken by hospital with treatment of colitis?

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital

indicators.note: treatment means handling or processing, so the letters of colitis are reworked

explanation.surface: Asking whether a hospital treats bowel inflammation by looking at the whole patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treatment of' is the anagram signal; read whole, the clue also describes an approach that treats the whole patient, not one organ.
explanation.definitionFit: Holistic medicine treats the whole person rather than one symptom, the approach the clue imagines.

clue.text: Hobbies interest them, or Ulster ministers wasting energy

parts.note: NI is Northern Ireland, often called Ulster

indicators.note: wasting means losing, so this letter drops out

parts.note: clergy ministers are trained theologians, or theologists
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Pastimes interest them, or else Northern Irish politicians squander power.
explanation.walkthrough: A hobby here is a small falcon, not a pastime. Ulster is the northern province of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Birdwatchers and bird scientists take interest in falcons such as the hobby.

clue.text: A big end and gear repaired here

definitions.text: A big end and gear repaired here

indicators.note: end means the final letter of big
repaired suggests the pieces are put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: A workshop where a car's big end and gearbox get fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: A big end is the part of an engine's connecting rod that joins the crankshaft.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor workshop is the place where vehicles and their parts are serviced and mended.

clue.text: Run into ragged urchin husband neglected

indicators.note: ragged means tattered and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone runs into a scruffy street child whose husband has been neglected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ragged' rearranges URCHIN, and 'neglected' says the H (husband) is left out of the result.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a cost or penalty is to bring it on oneself, to run into it.

clue.text: Panama City officer working his final passage

parts.note: COL is the abbreviation for colonel, an army officer
on means functioning or working

explanation.surface: A city official in Panama works on his final passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his final passage' is a second, cheeky definition: the bowel's last stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Colón is a port city on the Caribbean coast of Panama at the canal entrance.

clue.text: Poor service in London museum? On the contrary

indicators.note: in places the scrambled letters within the museum abbreviation

parts.note: the V and A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters of service are badly arranged

explanation.surface: A visitor complains of bad service at a London museum, then reverses the complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' scrambles SERVICE into ICEVERS, which goes 'in' V and A, the Victoria and Albert Museum.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase signals the reverse is true, the same as saying on the contrary.

clue.text: Old poet loses rare watch

indicators.note: loses means this letter is taken away

parts.note: Virgil was the ancient Roman poet

explanation.surface: An ancient poet mislays a valuable rare timepiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'watch' is a period of keeping awake, not a timepiece.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigil is a period of staying awake to keep guard or pray, so a watch.

clue.text: Group of relatives circulate key

indicators.note: circulate means go round, so the chosen letters are turned back
a group of the word means a run of its letters together

explanation.surface: A family group passes round a key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group of' takes LATIV from 'relatives'; 'circulate' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Key in the sense of essential or crucial, as in a key witness.

clue.text: Carpeting's total shambles without ruler

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the jumbled letters sit round the ruler
a shambles is a mess, so the letters of total are jumbled

parts.note: a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A carpet store is in total chaos with no boss present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking, and 'shambles' is the anagram signal. To be carpeted is to be summoned and scolded.
explanation.definitionFit: Being carpeted is being scolded by a superior, so carpeting means a reprimand or dressing-down.

clue.text: Start to tour America, taking in large city

indicators.note: start to means the opening letter of tour
taking in means the country letters hold another letter

parts.note: USA is the United States of America
L is the clothing size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Travel advice: begin your American tour by visiting a big city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulsa is a large city in Oklahoma in the United States.

clue.text: Set to screen golf for clubs

indicators.note: for means one letter stands in place of the other

parts.note: to screen something is to conceal it
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
Golf is G in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: Arranging to shield the golf course from the club members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps the C (clubs) in CONCEAL for G (golf).
explanation.definitionFit: Jelly that has set has thickened and solidified, which is to congeal.

clue.text: Train leaves around midnight for border

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters surround the midnight letter
to train is to shape or direct, so the letters of leaves are rearranged

parts.note: the middle of the word night is the letter G

explanation.surface: A train departs around midnight for the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' scrambles LEAVES into SELVAE, which goes 'around' G, the middle of 'night'.
explanation.definitionFit: A selvage is the finished edge of woven cloth, which stops it fraying, so it is a type of edging.
